articles.title: Ali G: Who Iz I? trailer reveals return of Sacha Baron Cohen’s prank-playing rudeboy
articles.summary: Comedian returns in new film, adding a retired US general to a list of pranked celebrities that include Buzz Aldrin and Donald Trump. The first full trailer for Ali G: Who Iz I?
body: Sporting new dreadlocks but still wearing the clothing that was favoured by young white Britons copying US hip-hop and Black streetwear fashions in the 00s, Ali is back to contend with the issues of the day – as well as the pregnancy of his long-term girlfriend, Julie. In the 20 years since the character has been away, he says that “the world went to crap: there was Covid, wars and Ed Sheeran”.
The trailer gives glimpses of pranks played on retired US army general Stewart Rodeheaver, and someone who may be the Canadian DJ and producer Deadmau5 at a music festival.

Ali G first appeared on the UK comedy programme The 11 O’Clock Show in 1998, then in three series of Da Ali G Show in the early 00s, during which he interviewed unsuspecting politicians, academics, public figures and celebrities. He asked Buzz Aldrin if man will ever walk on the sun (perhaps during winter when it’s cold) and pitched a business idea for “ice-cream gloves” to Donald Trump. Da Ali G Show also featured the first appearances of Baron Cohen’s other best-known characters: the Kazakh TV reporter Borat Sagdiyev, and Brüno, an obtuse Austrian fashionista.
points: Comedian returns in new film, adding a retired US general to a list of pranked celebrities that include Buzz Aldrin and Donald Trump.

articles.title: ‘Robocop’ TV Series Casts Dan Stevens in Lead Role
articles.summary: Dan Stevens is set for the title role in the “Robocop” TV series at Amazon Prime Video, Variety has confirmed. The show was originally announced in July at the streamer. Prime Video has given the show an eight-episode order.
body: Stevens broke out with his role in the hit British series “Downton Abbey,” with the actor going on to star in the critically-acclaimed show “Legion” at FX. His other TV roles include “Solar Opposites,” “Zero Day,” and the upcoming third season of AMC’s “The Terror.” He is also set for a series regular role in the upcoming second season of “Dexter: Resurrection.” In film, he recently starred in “Godzilla x Kong: New Empire” and is known for features like the live-action “Beauty and the Beast,” “Eurovision Song Contest: The Story of Fire Saga,” and “Cuckoo.”

Peter Ocko serves as writer, executive producer, and showrunner. James Wan, Michael Clear, and Rob Hackett executive produce via Blumhouse Atomic Monster. Michael Miner and Ed Neumeier, co-creators and co-writers of the original “Robocop” film, will also serve as executive producers. Danielle Bozzone of Blumhouse Atomic Monster will co-executive produce and oversee the project for the company. Amazon MGM Studios will produce.

articles.title: Andrew Garfield Opens Up About Playing Sam Altman in ‘Artificial,’ Says OpenAI Is Doing ‘Damage to the Soul of Humanity’
articles.summary: Andrew Garfield is opening up about stepping into the shoes of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman in Luca Guadagnino’s upcoming film “Artificial.” Garfield portrays the tech executive in the drama, which takes place during the five-day corporate saga in November 2023 that saw Altman abruptly fired as OpenAI CEO…
body: Garfield also said his usual acting process required him to look for elements of Altman within himself, including traits he might rather reject. He described the exercise using Carl Jung’s concept of “the shadow self,” or, as Garfield put it, “the aspects of ourselves that we disown.”
“There’s something there for me to integrate, because I’m so afraid of being it,” he said.

“But then the argument is, that if we weren’t all less rejecting in the first place, less ‘that’s not us’, then Donald Trump wouldn’t have been voted in twice, and Nigel Farage wouldn’t be anywhere near a position of power,” he continued. “Whereas if we go, ‘OK, interesting — where am I [in a] wannabe fascist, grifter, opportunist, power-hungry, ethic-less, spineless fucking pig?’ We can identify that this is the bad part of us. We know this in ourselves.”

“Artificial,” written by Simon Rich, also stars Monica Barbaro as former OpenAI chief technology officer Mira Murati, Yura Borisov as OpenAI co-founder and former chief scientist Ilya Sutskever and Ike Barinholtz as Elon Musk. Cooper Hoffman, Jason Schwartzman, Billie Lourd, Zosia Mamet, Chris O’Dowd and Mark Rylance round out the ensemble.

articles.title: ‘Dunkman’: How Shaquille O’Neal Made Dunk Contests Great Again
articles.summary: Shaquille O’Neal loves solving problems. The basketball icon and four-time NBA champion, 54, has two master’s degrees, a doctorate, served as a sheriff’s deputy and honorary U.S. Marshal, and once played for Doc Rivers.
body: He began hounding Colin Smeeton, his longtime manager and business partner, about meeting the owner of Ring and investing in the company. The following January, O’Neal made a beeline for Ring founder Jamie Siminoff at CES, the annual tech trade show in Las Vegas, telling him, “I’d love to find a way to partner with you but I don’t want to just be a pitchman; I want to have equity in the company.” So, O’Neal was granted what Smeeton calls “a sizable equity stake in the company” that made him millions when it sold to Amazon for $1.15 billion a year later.
“He’s constantly challenging himself and always looking for what the new opportunity is,” Smeeton says.

It had been close to a decade since the annual All-Star Weekend competition was any good (see: Zach LaVine vs. Aaron Gordon, 2016), and a quarter-century removed from the last bona fide NBA superstar participating in it (Vince Carter, 2000). The days of Michael Jordan and Kobe Bryant soaring through the air were long gone.

This season drew strong audiences for CNN, and ranked among the top drivers of new CNN All Access subscriptions in June during its premiere.
The 78th Emmy Awards air live Monday, Sept. 14, from 8 p.m. to 11 p.m. ET on NBC and streaming on Peacock.

articles.title: Penny Lane Is Dead review – Aussie slasher comedy zips from Neighbours to nasty
articles.summary: Mia’Kate Russell’s 80s-set Ozsploitation horror is a tad slapdash, but the grungy gore and seething catfights save it from dud status. Here is a muddled if energetic effort from Australian writer-director Mia’Kate Russell.
body: Set in Australia in 1986 (presumably because this means no mobile phones, and thus no calling for help), a trio of high-school besties prepares for a night of partying before the summer ends. Penny (Bailey Spalding) is planning to go to university to study law and asks her girlfriend Toni (Tahlee Fereday) to come with her. The two have only recently become lovers and they haven’t yet come out to their buddy Amy (Alexandra Jensen) – a sweet, childlike teen who still carries a stuffed tiger toy around for comfort.

And they most certainly haven’t come out to Kat (Sophia Wright-Mendelsohn, daughter of Aussie actor Ben Mendelsohn) – an erstwhile friend with whom they haven’t hung out for a while and who they didn’t think would show up that evening. Except here she is, bearing cupcakes for each of them with insults piped on the top in icing. Kat, it turns out, has drugged Penny’s cake, so she passes out and Kat’s super-skeevy ex-con boyfriend Angus (Ben O’Toole) shows up with his leather-clad crew – and suddenly it all goes from an episode of Neighbours to The Last House on the Left.
points: Mia’Kate Russell’s 80s-set Ozsploitation horror is a tad slapdash, but the grungy gore and seething catfights save it from dud status.

articles.title: Zip Wire review – cancer-curing scientist is on the hook for cable-dangle thriller
articles.summary: This nonsensical film sees an OCD-afflicted scientist fending off assassins while hanging from an aerial wire, and fails to get pulses racing for even a minute. In this silly, low-adrenaline thriller, the title star is a rickety old zip wire bolted into the side of a mountain in the Italian…
body: The scientist is Amy (MyAnna Buring); she has discovered a cure for lung cancer, and her drive is explained in syrupy hospital-ward flashbacks to her mother dying when she was a teenager. Amy also has OCD – she is so anxious about germs that she never takes off her rubber gloves, and has an assistant in her lab to do anything that involves touching or handling objects. (Like all the characters, she never gets beyond a stereotype.) Her research is bankrolled by a big pharma company, whose CEO is played by Saffron Burrows (now seemingly mandatory casting for ropey British thrillers).

Amy’s gamechanging discoveries result in an old-school conspiracy, involving a notebook with her research written in code and a trio of contract killers. Which is how Amy ends up in the Dolomites (where everyone has an English accent), halfway across a zip line. Supposedly, a human body cannot remain in a state of maximum panic for more than 30 minutes, but Amy seems to bat away her terrible fear of heights in about five minutes flat. For the audience, you’ll be lucky if this gets your pulse racing for more than two of them.

articles.title: 'Obsessive' Billie Piper stalker jailed for 12 months
articles.summary: Philip Jerome admits breaching a stalking prevention order designed to protect the ex-Doctor Who star.
body: An "obsessive" fan with a "sexual interest" in Billie Piper has been jailed for 12 months for breaching a stalking prevention order designed to protect the ex-pop singer and Doctor Who star.
Philip Jerome, of Winchester, Hampshire, appeared at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court on his 49th birthday after pleading guilty to four breach charges.

The court heard police carried out an inspection of his devices on 27 December, finding four images of Piper saved on his phone, and that he had tagged 11 posts and images on X relating to her on four days that month.
Defence lawyer Caroline Bonavia said he had had a recent autism diagnosis and had sought psychological support over "obsessive" relationships.
points: Philip Jerome admits breaching a stalking prevention order designed to protect the ex-Doctor Who star.

articles.title: Kate Hudson to make How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days sequel, 23 years on
articles.summary: Hudson and Matthew McConaughey, her co-star from the 2003 rom-com, could be reunited for the sequel.
body: A sequel to How to Lose a Guy In 10 Days is in development, more than 20 years after the original hit rom-com was released, with original star Kate Hudson set to produce.
Work on the film is in the "very early days", with sources telling US media, external that both Hudson, 47, and Matthew McConaughey, 56, could reprise their roles from the first film.

In the original, Hudson played a magazine journalist called Andie who researches an article about modern dating. She convinces her boss she can get a man, Benjamin (McConaughey), to leave her in 10 days. Meanwhile, Benjamin bets his boss he can make any woman fall for him, with Andie his target.
Hudson will produce the sequel alongside Stacey Sher, who is behind hits such as Pulp Fiction and Matilda.
points: Hudson and Matthew McConaughey, her co-star from the 2003 rom-com, could be reunited for the sequel.

articles.title: Awards Categories Set for Cannes-Winning ‘All of a Sudden’ Actresses Virginie Efira and Tao Okamoto (Exclusive)
articles.summary: Neon, which will release Ryusuke Hamaguchi's French-language film in the U.S., will push Efira, who plays the director of a Paris nursing home in the film, for best actress, and Okamoto, who plays a terminally-ill Japanese playwright, for best supporting actress.
body: Virginie Efira and Tao Okamoto, who shared the best actress prize at May’s Cannes Film Festival for their performances in Japanese auteur Ryusuke Hamaguchi ’s French-language debut All of a Sudden, will not be pitted against one another this awards season, The Hollywood Reporter has exclusively learned.

The distributor, which has guided a considerable number of non-English-language films to major awards recognition, including Parasite, The Worst Person in the World and Anatomy of a Fall, will also campaign for All of a Sudden in picture, director and adapted screenplay categories. It remains to be seen if France or Japan will submit the film for the best international feature Oscar race.

Okamoto who became the first Japanese actress ever honored with Cannes’ best actress prize, just gave birth and is therefore less available to travel than Efira. Efira recently collected an honor at the Locarno Film Festival in Switzerland; made a swing through Los Angeles for screenings, tastemaker events and an intimate lunch with journalists; and will soon be headed to the Toronto and New York film festivals — the latter with Hamaguchi — to help launch the film in North America.
